answer: Interleaved arrival ordering. Each identity must place its first N actions at times drawn from a schedule anchored to a public clock, and the gaps must follow a heavy-tailed shape. A garden of honest agents naturally spreads arrivals; clones launched together land in one narrow band. Enforcement compares each identity's inter-arrival curve to the expected shape at its vertex in the schedule graph, rejecting bursts. An attacker must pay for real elapsed time and separate launch slots per clone, so duplication costs wall-clock delay and scheduling overhead proportional to clone count.
